lesson.title: What Is Simran? A Quiet, Peaceful Heart
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: Have you ever sat quietly and felt really calm and peaceful? In Sikhi, taking quiet moments to remember and feel close to Waheguru (God) is called Simran. Today we'll practice a simple, quiet moment of Simran together.

Simran doesn't have to be complicated. It can be as simple as sitting quietly, breathing slowly, and thinking peaceful thoughts. Try this with your grown-up: sit comfortably, close your eyes if that feels good, take three slow breaths, and quietly think the word 'Waheguru' in your mind. Notice how your body feels calmer afterward.
That quiet, peaceful feeling is what Simran helps build. This week, try one quiet moment of Simran on your own, even just for a few breaths.

objectives: Explain in simple words what Simran means (quietly remembering and feeling close to Waheguru)
Practice a short, guided moment of quiet remembrance
materialsNeeded: A quiet space for the practice moment
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child to describe a time they felt really calm and peaceful.
2. Introduce Simran as taking quiet moments to remember and feel close to Waheguru.
3. Guide a short practice moment together: sit comfortably, take three slow breaths, quietly think 'Waheguru.'
4. Talk about how their body felt afterward — calmer, slower, quieter.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace the word and talk through its meaning again.
6. Close by picking one time this week to try a quiet Simran moment on their own.
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep the quiet moment very short (even 10-15 seconds) — the goal is a positive first experience, not a long practice
Ready for more: introduce that Simran often happens through Nitnem (daily prayers), which they'll learn more about in later lessons
For a child who finds sitting still hard, try a slow, quiet walk instead of sitting — the calm, mindful quality matters more than the position
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and experiential activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing. Check that the child can describe Simran as a quiet, peaceful remembrance in their own words.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Simran is one of the foundational, universally-taught values of Sikhi alongside Seva and Sangat (introduced in the previous lesson) — introducing it experientially, through an actual quiet moment, builds real understanding before more abstract doctrinal study in later grades.

generationData.instructions: Trace the word, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
